title: Flags
description:
Write four functions on permission flags stored as bits of an integer, using the bitwise operators:

```lua
FLAGS = { read = 1, write = 2, exec = 4, hidden = 8 }

grant(perms, name)     -- the permissions with that flag set
revoke(perms, name)    -- with it cleared
has(perms, name)       -- true or false
describe(perms)        -- "rwx-" style: r, w, x, h for each set flag in that order, "-" for each clear one
```

An unknown flag name raises an error.

starter.solution.lua:
FLAGS = { read = 1, write = 2, exec = 4, hidden = 8 }

function grant(perms, name) return perms end
function revoke(perms, name) return perms end
function has(perms, name) return false end
function describe(perms) return "----" end

solution.solution.lua:
FLAGS = { read = 1, write = 2, exec = 4, hidden = 8 }

local function flag(name)
    local bit = FLAGS[name]
    if not bit then error("unknown flag: " .. tostring(name), 3) end
    return bit
end

function grant(perms, name) return perms | flag(name) end
function revoke(perms, name) return perms & ~flag(name) end
function has(perms, name) return perms & flag(name) ~= 0 end

function describe(perms)
    local out = {}
    for _, pair in ipairs({ { "read", "r" }, { "write", "w" }, { "exec", "x" }, { "hidden", "h" } }) do
        out[#out + 1] = perms & FLAGS[pair[1]] ~= 0 and pair[2] or "-"
    end
    return table.concat(out)
end

hints: Set a flag with `perms | bit`, clear it with `perms & ~bit`, test it with `perms & bit ~= 0` (in Lua the comparison binds more loosely than `&`, so no brackets are needed).
unitTests:
test("granting and revoking", function()
    local p = 0
    p = grant(p, "read")
    p = grant(p, "exec")
    check_eq(p, 5)
    check_eq(has(p, "read"), true)
    check_eq(has(p, "write"), false)
    p = revoke(p, "read")
    p = revoke(p, "read")
    check_eq(p, 4)
    check_eq(describe(grant(p, "hidden")), "--xh")
    check_eq(describe(15), "rwxh")
    check_eq(describe(0), "----")
end)

test("unknown flags", function()
    check_error(grant, 0, "delete")
    check_error(has, 0, "nope")
end)
